# Bucket archiving and query-based reopening
Source: https://llms-explorer.com/tree/bucket-archiving-and-query-based-reopening/

# Bucket archiving and query-based reopening — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Bucket archiving and query-based reopening. Run status: COMPLETED.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-31 · budgeted to ≈8000 tokens; the full catalogue is llms-full.txt -->

## How it works

- [statement] Bucket reopening belongs to the insertion path: when no suitable open bucket exists, the catalog can return either an archived bucket’s _id or query filters. After retrieving the bucket from disk, MongoDB recreates its in-memory representation. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md
- [statement] When an insert lacks a suitable open bucket, reopening can identify an archived bucket by _id or search disk using a query. The implementation checks for an archive candidate before considering query-based reopening. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp
- [statement] In checkForReopeningConflict, query-based reopening conflicts with any outstanding reopening for the same BucketKey. Archive-based reopening conflicts with query-based reopening for that key or another archive reopening of the same bucket, allowing narrower synchronization when the bucket identity is known. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82090

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Finding a candidate on disk does not guarantee successful reopening. SERVER-102677 describes checks before a candidate returns to catalog memory and names era mismatch, hash collision and malformed buckets as failure reasons. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-10) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-102677
- [statement] OneUptime describes late or out-of-order inserts as potentially reopening closed buckets or creating new small buckets and reducing compression efficiency. Its article supplies no measured universal reopening penalty; treat the performance warning as qualitative. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-12) — https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-03-31-mongodb-time-series-compression/view
- [statement] The implementation disables query-based reopening after a rollover reason other than kTimeBackward; once disabled for that decision flow it cannot be re-enabled. Reopening eligibility therefore does not mean every rollover triggers a disk query. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/bucket_catalog/bucket_catalog.cpp
- [statement] SERVER-102677 explains that an on-disk candidate must pass checks before returning to catalog memory, including checks for era mismatch, hash collision and malformed buckets. Its issue record lists finer failure counters as fixed in 8.2.0-rc0; counter availability must be checked against the deployed release. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-04-10) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-102677
- [statement] SERVER-99527 documents a historical failure where measurement deletes changed control.min without changing the bucket _id timestamp, allowing query-based reopening beyond the original bucket span. Its advisory lists 7.0.0–7.0.15 and 8.0.0–8.0.3 as affected, with fixes in 7.0.16 and 8.0.4. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-07) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-99527

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The implementation README says query-based reopening requires a {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} index and is not used when that index is absent. It dates automatic creation of that index for new time-series collections to version 6.3; this requirement concerns the query path rather than the direct archived-_id path. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Archiving removes most of a bucket’s in-memory catalog state but retains a small record for efficient reopening. If memory pressure persists after eligible open buckets have been archived, the catalog can remove archived entries; buckets removed this way remain eligible for query-based reopening. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md
- [statement] For a collection with a metaField, query-based reopening filters for an exact metadata match, a matching time range, capacity under timeseriesBucketMaxCount and timeseriesBucketMaxSize, and control.closed absent or false. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md
- [statement] Catalog eviction does not necessarily permanently close a bucket: after its archived record is removed, the on-disk bucket can remain eligible for query-based reopening. Setting control.closed to true instead excludes reopening. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md
- [statement] Archive-based reopening knows the target bucket identifier, while query-based reopening operates on a series. MongoDB’s synchronization issue SERVER-82090 explicitly uses that distinction to propose narrower conflicts for archive-based reopening. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-82090
- [statement] A MongoDB-authored bitemporal case study chose transactionTime as its timeField to avoid historical backfills that would require reopening old buckets. This is a workload-specific design example, not proof that every late insert fails or that reopening is always harmful. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-31) — https://medium.com/mongodb/mongodb-a-case-study-in-bitemporal-data-management-addressing-challenges-in-high-frequency-2417419f1500
- [statement] Archiving discards most in-memory bucket state but retains a compact reopening record. SERVER-66683 describes retaining the BucketKey hash and bucket _id; the bucket remains eligible for additional measurements. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-66683
- [statement] For collections with a metaField, the documented query path requires a {metaField: 1, timeField: 1} index; its absence disables that path. SERVER-95067 identifies {timeField: 1} as the corresponding index for collections without metadata. (medium confidence) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mongodb/mongo/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Bucket archiving and query-based reopening · also: https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95067
- [statement] serverStatus separates numBucketsFetched, archived candidates fetched for suitability checks, from numBucketsQueried, candidates queried for an incoming document. numBucketFetchesFailed and numBucketQueriesFailed distinguish unsuitable fetched candidates from queries with no candidate; numBucketsReopened records successful reuse. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-30) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverstatus/
- [statement] SERVER-95067 documents a historical lost-document defect requiring retryable, unordered multi-document inserts, concurrent insertion into the same bucket, and the reopening index. The advisory limits affected releases to 7.0.0–7.0.15 and 8.0.0–8.0.3 and identifies fixes in 7.0.16 and 8.0.4. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-01-29) — https://jira.mongodb.org/browse/SERVER-95067
